q21452.en: The sign shown indicates that to reach Milan you must continue straight on.

explain.short: The arrow under MILANO goes straight up, so for Milan you keep straight on.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'proseguire diritto' (continue straight on) matches the straight arrow.

q21453.en: The sign shown indicates two specific destinations.

explain.short: It names two places: Milano (straight on) and the town centre (to the right).
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'due determinate destinazioni' (two specific destinations): count them, Milano and centro.

q21454.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of a junction with a right turn for the town centre.

explain.short: The arrow for 'centro' bends to the right, so at the junction ahead you turn right for the centre.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'centro cittadino' (town centre) is the word 'centro' with the target symbol.

sceneParams.caption: Centro: turn right at the junction

keywords.en: warns in advance of a junction

q21455.en: The sign shown can be found on urban roads.

explain.short: The white background is used for direction signs on urban roads (inside towns).
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'si può trovare' (can be found) only says it is possible, and white means urban.

q21456.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of a junction where you must continue straight on to go to Milan.

explain.short: It stands before a junction, and the straight arrow shows the way to Milano.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'preavvisa' (warns in advance): the junction is a little further ahead.

keywords.en: warns in advance of a junction

q21457.en: The sign shown is found only on one-way roads.

explain.short: This direction sign can stand on any urban road, one-way or two-way.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: nothing on the sign talks about one-way traffic.

sceneParams.caption: Not only one-way roads: any town road

q21458.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of a junction for the shooting range.

explain.short: The target symbol next to 'centro' means the town centre, not a shooting range.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: The round 'target' symbol is the town-centre symbol, not 'poligono di tiro a segno' (shooting range).

sceneParams.caption: Target symbol = town centre, not shooting

q21459.en: The sign shown indicates that by turning right you meet a secondary road.

explain.short: Turning right takes you to the town centre; the sign says nothing about a secondary road.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'strada secondaria' (secondary road) is invented: the right arrow leads to 'centro'.

sceneParams.caption: Right = town centre, not a side road

q21460.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of the end of two-way traffic and the start of one-way traffic.

explain.short: It is a direction sign with place names; it says nothing about one-way or two-way traffic.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'fine del doppio senso' (end of two-way traffic) has nothing to do with arrows to places.

sceneParams.caption: Directions to places, not one-way traffic

q21461.en: The sign shown tells you to turn right to reach a shopping centre.

explain.short: 'centro' with the target symbol is the town centre, not a shopping centre.
explain.rule: A white sign with arrows announces a junction in town: Milano is straight on, the town centre is to the right.
explain.trap: 'centro commerciale' (shopping centre) is a trap on the word 'centro'.

sceneParams.caption: Centro = town centre, not shopping centre

q21462.en: The sign shown is found on main extra-urban roads.

explain.short: Exit signs on a blue background are used on main extra-urban roads (dual carriageways outside towns).
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'extraurbane principali' (main extra-urban roads) = blue; motorways would be green.

sceneParams.caption: Blue exit sign = main extra-urban road

q21463.en: The sign shown indicates that the exit junction for Frosinone is 500 metres away.

explain.short: The top says 'uscita FROSINONE' and the bottom says '500 m': the exit is 500 m ahead.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'svincolo di uscita' (exit junction) is what is 500 m away, not the town.

q21464.en: The sign shown gives the names of the places you can reach by leaving the main extra-urban road.

explain.short: The middle part lists places (Ceccano, Priverno, Terracina...) reached by taking this exit.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'uscendo' (by leaving): these places are reached after the exit.

q21465.en: The sign shown indicates the tourist places with the writing on a brown background.

explain.short: Circeo and Campocatino are written on brown boxes: brown marks tourist places.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'fondo marrone' (brown background) is the tourist colour.

q21466.en: The sign shown indicates the distance between the sign and the next exit junction.

explain.short: The '500 m' at the bottom is how far it is from the sign to the exit.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'distanza ... prossimo svincolo' (distance to the next exit) = the 500 m.

sceneParams.caption: 500 m from the sign to the exit

q21467.en: The sign shown is found when leaving the town of Frosinone.

explain.short: It stands on the main road before the exit for Frosinone, not where you leave the town.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'uscendo dal comune' (leaving the town) mixes up 'uscita' (road exit) with leaving a town.

sceneParams.caption: Before the road exit, not leaving the town

q21468.en: The sign shown indicates that in 500 metres you arrive at the town of Frosinone.

explain.short: In 500 m you reach the EXIT named Frosinone, not the town itself.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'si arriva al comune' (you arrive at the town) is wrong: 500 m is to the exit.

sceneParams.caption: 500 m to the exit, not to the town

q21469.en: The sign shown indicates that all the places on the sign are 500 metres away.

explain.short: Only the exit is 500 m away; the places are further on, after the exit.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'tutte le località' (all the places) is the trap: 500 m is the exit only.

sceneParams.caption: Only the exit is 500 m away

q21470.en: The sign shown indicates that the road can no longer be used and that the last exit is Frosinone.

explain.short: It only announces the next exit; the road goes on after it.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'non è più percorribile' (can no longer be used) and 'ultima uscita' (last exit) are invented.

q21471.en: The sign shown indicates the start of a built-up area.

explain.short: A town's start is a white sign with the town name; this is a blue exit sign.
explain.rule: Blue sign 'uscita': the exit to Frosinone is 500 m ahead; it lists the places you reach from that exit, brown = tourist places.
explain.trap: 'inizio di un centro abitato' (start of a built-up area) has a different, white sign.

sceneParams.caption: Exit sign, not the start of a town

q21472.en: The sign shown indicates the end of the built-up area.

explain.short: The town name crossed by a red bar means you are leaving the town.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'fine' (end): the red bar across the name always means end.

sceneParams.caption: Red bar on the name = end of town

q21473.en: The sign shown, in the first line at the top of the blue panel, indicates the next built-up area.

explain.short: The places are listed from nearest to furthest, so S. Cesareo (7 km) on top is the next town.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'prima riga in alto' (first line at the top) = the nearest place.

q21474.en: The sign shown indicates the end of the built-up area and the places that follow.

explain.short: The top part says the town ends; the blue panel shows the next places.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'e le località successive' (and the next places) is the blue panel.

q21475.en: The sign shown, in the blue panel, indicates for each place its distance in kilometres.

explain.short: The number next to each name (7, 63, 190) is its distance in km.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'distanza chilometrica' (distance in km): the numbers are km, not road numbers.

q21476.en: The sign shown indicates that Naples is 190 kilometres away.

explain.short: Next to NAPOLI is 190: Naples is 190 km away.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'mancano' (are left): 190 is the km still to drive.

q21477.en: The sign shown indicates that S. Cesareo is 7 kilometres away.

explain.short: Next to S. CESAREO is 7: it is 7 km away.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'mancano 7 chilometri' (7 km to go) matches the number.

q21478.en: The sign shown indicates the start of an uphill stretch of road to reach Montecompatri.

explain.short: The red bar means the end of the town Montecompatri; it says nothing about a slope.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'in salita' (uphill) is invented: a slope has its own red-triangle danger sign.

sceneParams.caption: End of town, not an uphill road

q21479.en: The sign shown indicates that it is not possible to reach Montecompatri.

explain.short: You are just leaving Montecompatri; the red bar is not a ban.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'non è possibile raggiungere' (cannot be reached): the red bar means end of town, not 'closed'.

keywords.en: it is not possible to reach

q21480.en: The sign shown indicates that to reach Naples you must drive along state road no. 190.

explain.short: 190 is the distance in km to Napoli, not the number of a road.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'strada statale n. 190' (state road no. 190) is the trap: road numbers are not shown here.

sceneParams.caption: 190 = km to Napoli, not a road number

q21481.en: The sign shown indicates a road closed to traffic.

explain.short: It shows the end of a town and the next places; the road is open.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'chiusa al traffico' (closed to traffic): the red bar is not a 'no entry' sign.

sceneParams.caption: End of town, road is open

q21482.en: The sign shown is found on main extra-urban roads.

explain.short: It stands where an ordinary road leaves a town; main extra-urban roads do not cross towns.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'extraurbane principali' (main extra-urban roads) have no town-end signs on them.

sceneParams.caption: On a road leaving a town, not a main road

q21483.en: The sign shown indicates the start of the built-up area.

explain.short: The red bar across the name means the END of the town, not the start.
explain.rule: Red bar on the name = end of the town; the blue panel lists the next places with their distance in km.
explain.trap: 'inizio' (start) vs 'fine' (end): the red bar always means end.

q21484.en: The sign shown indicates the start of a pedestrian area.

explain.short: It says 'area pedonale' with a pedestrian symbol: here the pedestrian area begins.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'area pedonale' (pedestrian area) is written on the sign itself.

q21485.en: The sign shown indicates, in the extra panel, the vehicles that may enter.

explain.short: The lower panel starts with 'eccetto' (except) and lists the vehicles allowed in.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'pannello aggiuntivo' (extra panel) is the lower part with the list.

q21486.en: The sign shown allows vehicles to drive in for loading and unloading goods.

explain.short: The panel lets authorised goods vehicles in, at the hours shown, to load and unload.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'carico e scarico merci' (loading and unloading goods) is one of the exceptions on the panel.

sceneParams.caption: Goods vehicles may enter at set hours

q21487.en: The sign shown allows vehicles for disabled people to drive in.

explain.short: The panel shows the wheelchair symbol: vehicles serving disabled people may enter.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'persone diversamente abili' (disabled people) = the wheelchair symbol in the panel.

sceneParams.caption: Vehicles for disabled people may enter

q21488.en: The sign shown indicates a police station.

explain.short: It marks a pedestrian area; police vehicles are only one of the exceptions.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'stazione di polizia' (police station): the police symbol is just in the list of exceptions.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrian area, not a police station

q21489.en: The sign shown indicates an area reserved only for disabled people.

explain.short: It is an area for pedestrians; disabled people's vehicles are one exception among several.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: the panel lists other vehicles too.

sceneParams.caption: For pedestrians, not only disabled people

q21490.en: The sign shown indicates police on foot.

explain.short: The walking person is a pedestrian: it is a pedestrian area.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'polizia a piedi' (police on foot): the figure is any pedestrian, not an officer.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrian figure, not police on foot

q21491.en: The sign shown indicates street sellers.

explain.short: It marks a pedestrian area; it says nothing about street sellers.
explain.rule: 'area pedonale' = start of a pedestrian area; the 'eccetto' panel lists the vehicles still allowed in.
explain.trap: 'venditori ambulanti' (street sellers) is invented.

q21492.en: The sign shown indicates the start of a limited traffic zone.

explain.short: The sign reads 'zona traffico limitato': the ZTL starts here.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'zona a traffico limitato' (limited traffic zone) is written on the sign.

sceneParams.caption: Start of a limited traffic zone (ZTL)

q21493.en: The sign shown indicates the start of the area where traffic is allowed only for some categories of vehicles.

explain.short: In a ZTL only the vehicles listed on the panel may drive in.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'solo ad alcune categorie' (only for some categories) is exactly what 'limited' means.

sceneParams.caption: Only some vehicle categories may enter

keywords.it: solo ad alcune categorie di veicoli
keywords.en: only for some categories of vehicles

q21494.en: The sign shown states which vehicles may enter.

explain.short: After 'eccetto' (except) the panel lists the vehicles allowed in.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'possono entrare' (may enter) = the list after 'eccetto'.

q21495.en: The sign shown states the categories of vehicles allowed through.

explain.short: The panel names the categories admitted: disabled people's vehicles, emergency vehicles, goods vehicles.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'ammessi al transito' (allowed through) = the exceptions on the panel.

q21496.en: The sign shown indicates a one-way road.

explain.short: It marks a limited traffic zone; one-way has a different blue sign with a white arrow.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) has nothing to do with the red-ringed disc.

q21497.en: The sign shown bans all vehicles from driving through.

explain.short: The ban has exceptions: the vehicles listed after 'eccetto' may enter.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) is the trap: some categories are admitted.

sceneParams.caption: Not all vehicles banned: exceptions apply

q21498.en: The sign shown indicates a military zone.

explain.short: It marks a limited traffic zone in a town, not a military area.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'zona militare' (military zone): 'zona' here is 'zona traffico limitato'.

q21499.en: The sign shown indicates that the road is closed because of heavy traffic.

explain.short: Access is limited to some vehicles by rule, not because of heavy traffic.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'intenso traffico' (heavy traffic) is a trap on the word 'traffico'.

sceneParams.caption: Limited access, not closed for traffic

q21500.en: The sign shown allows only residents to drive through.

explain.short: The panel admits categories like disabled people's vehicles, emergency and goods vehicles, not 'residents only'.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'solo ai residenti' (only residents) is the trap: the panel does not say that.

q21501.en: The sign shown indicates the start of a pedestrian area.

explain.short: It reads 'zona traffico limitato' with a red-ringed disc; a pedestrian area has a pedestrian symbol.
explain.rule: 'zona traffico limitato' = start of a ZTL: only the vehicle categories listed on the panel may enter.
explain.trap: 'area pedonale' (pedestrian area) is a different sign, with the walking person.

q21502.en: The sign shown lets you know the transit conditions of the Stelvio pass.

explain.short: It tells you whether the Stelvio pass is open or closed and what equipment you need.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'condizioni di transitabilità' (transit conditions) is the name of this type of sign.

q21503.en: The sign shown indicates that you must drive only with chains or winter tyres.

explain.short: The tyre-with-chains symbol under 'aperto' means chains or winter tyres are needed.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'necessario' (necessary) and 'solo' (only): here it is a requirement, not advice.

sceneParams.caption: Only with chains or winter tyres

q21504.en: The sign shown indicates that the road is open, but only to vehicles equipped with chains or winter tyres.

explain.short: 'aperto' says the road is open; the symbol limits it to vehicles with chains or winter tyres.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'aperta, ma solo' (open, but only): both parts are on the sign.

sceneParams.caption: Open, but only with chains/winter tyres

q21505.en: The sign shown is placed on mountain roads.

explain.short: It gives the conditions of a mountain pass, so it stands on mountain roads.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'strade di montagna' (mountain roads): Stelvio is a high mountain pass.

q21506.en: The sign shown indicates that it is possible to reach the Stelvio pass.

explain.short: The pass is 'aperto' (open), so you can reach it (with chains or winter tyres).
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'aperto' (open) = it is possible to reach the pass.

sceneParams.caption: Pass open: you can reach it

q21507.en: The sign shown indicates the road is open only to vehicles with new tyres.

explain.short: It asks for chains or winter tyres, not new tyres.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'pneumatici nuovi' (new tyres) is the trap: the symbol means chains or winter tyres.

sceneParams.caption: Chains or winter tyres, not new tyres

q21508.en: The sign shown advises fitting the chains.

explain.short: Here chains or winter tyres are required, not just advised.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'consiglia' (advises) is too weak: it is a requirement.

q21509.en: The sign shown requires fitting chains on all four wheels.

explain.short: It asks for chains OR winter tyres, and says nothing about all four wheels.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'su tutte le quattro ruote' (on all four wheels) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Chains or winter tyres, not four wheels

q21510.en: The sign shown requires removing the chains so as not to damage the road surface.

explain.short: It is the opposite: you need chains or winter tyres to go on.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'togliere le catene' (remove the chains) is the opposite of the sign.

sceneParams.caption: Opposite: chains or winter tyres needed

q21511.en: The sign shown indicates the opening of a ski lift.

explain.short: 'aperto' refers to the Stelvio pass road, not to a ski facility.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass is open, but only for vehicles with snow chains or winter tyres.
explain.trap: 'impianto sciistico' (ski lift): 'aperto' is about the road.

sceneParams.caption: Road open, not a ski lift

q21512.en: The sign shown advises proceeding with special care and attention.

explain.short: The pass is closed and the road to Trafoi may have snow, so you drive carefully.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'consiglia ... prudenza' (advises care) fits a sign about snow and a closed pass.

q21513.en: The sign shown indicates that the Stelvio pass cannot be reached.

explain.short: The red panel says 'chiuso' (closed): the pass cannot be reached.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'non è raggiungibile' (cannot be reached) = 'chiuso' in red.

q21514.en: The sign shown recommends using chains or winter tyres as far as Trafoi.

explain.short: The chains symbols with 'fino a TRAFOI' show that up to Trafoi chains or winter tyres are recommended.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'raccomanda' (recommends) and 'fino a' (as far as) both come from the lower panel.

q21514.reviewNote: Official answer treats the chains symbol here as advice; the transitability sign rule (and group 4294) treats it as compulsory. Check.

q21515.en: The sign shown indicates that it is possible to go as far as Trafoi.

explain.short: 'fino a TRAFOI' (as far as Trafoi): the road is open up to Trafoi.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'fino a' (as far as) marks how far you can go.

q21516.en: The sign shown indicates that the service stations are closed.

explain.short: 'chiuso' refers to the Stelvio pass, not to petrol stations.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'stazioni di servizio' (service stations) are not on this sign.

q21517.en: The sign shown indicates that fitting winter tyres is compulsory.

explain.short: For the quiz, chains or winter tyres are only recommended up to Trafoi, not compulsory.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'obbligatorio' (compulsory) is the trap: the quiz reads this sign as a recommendation.

q21517.reviewNote: Official answer treats the chains symbol here as advice; the transitability sign rule (and group 4294) treats it as compulsory. Check.

q21518.en: The sign shown bans vehicles without snow chains from driving through.

explain.short: It does not ban anyone: it closes the pass and recommends chains up to Trafoi.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'vieta' (bans) is too strong: there is no ban sign here.

q21518.reviewNote: Official answer treats the chains symbol here as advice; the transitability sign rule (and group 4294) treats it as compulsory. Check.

q21519.en: The sign shown indicates that, to drive through, vehicles must carry chains on board.

explain.short: For the quiz the sign recommends chains or winter tyres; it does not make carrying chains a condition.
explain.rule: Mountain sign: Stelvio pass closed; you can drive up to Trafoi, with chains or winter tyres recommended.
explain.trap: 'debbono avere a bordo' (must carry on board) turns a recommendation into an obligation.

q21519.reviewNote: Official answer treats the chains symbol here as advice; the transitability sign rule (and group 4294) treats it as compulsory. Check.
